summary: The note reports on Hurricane Elara, a Category 5 storm that struck San Juan, Puerto Rico on October 10, killing 47 people and crippling infrastructure. It covers individual stories of loss and heroism, political criticism of the aid response, concerns about slow aid delivery, long-neglected infrastructure, climate change as a driver of stronger storms, and the economic and policy outlook for rebuilding.
one_line: Hurricane Elara, a Category 5 storm, devastated San Juan on October 10, killing 47 and prompting political fallout, aid concerns, and resilience debates.
key_facts: Hurricane Elara passed through San Juan, Puerto Rico on October 10, two days before the article's reporting.
Elara reached Category 5 status at landfall, with winds exceeding 160 mph and a storm surge that inundated coastal areas.
The death toll stood at 47, and officials feared many people were missing.
Mayor Carmen Torres said the focus should be "search, rescue, and rebuilding."
Luis Rivera, a father of two, sheltered his family in a storm shelter minutes before their home was devastated; he said "All that matters is we're still together."
Dr Adriana Vega helped deliver a baby by flashlight as the local hospital ran on an overtaxed generator.
Opposition leader Manuel Serrano cited Elara as evidence of "deep-seated neglect" of disaster-prone areas by the current administration, despite promises to modernize infrastructure.
Survivors protested delays in aid distribution and what many consider inadequate emergency preparedness.
Red Cross coordinator Sofia Mendoza said "We need more hands, more supplies, and more urgency"; multiple countries pledged resources, but logistics slowed the response.
San Juan's infrastructure was already stressed by budget cuts and postponed maintenance.
Dr. Gabriela Ruiz of the University of Puerto Rico's Department of Climatology said storms feed off warmer ocean temperatures and that what was once unprecedented has become normalized.
Schools are closed, businesses destroyed, and cultural landmarks damaged in San Juan.
Economic impacts include rebuilding costs, lost tourism revenue, and trade disruptions affecting San Juan's fragile economy.
Legislators are holding emergency sessions on disaster preparedness, climate change mitigation, and infrastructure policy.
